one_line_description: Small-molecule macrophage reprogramming for solid tumors.

founder.narrative: Dr. Marisol Reyes presents as a credible scientific operator: twelve years at Genentech and two INDs led is a real, checkable claim, and it maps directly to the company's next milestone, which is IND-enabling toxicology. What the deck does not show is company-building. There is no evidence she has hired outside her function, carried a P&L, closed a financing, or run a commercial negotiation. Founder-market fit on the science is strong; founder-market fit on the business of a venture-backed biotech is unproven.

strengths.claim: CEO has directly relevant drug-development experience at a top-tier biotech.
strengths.quote: Dr. Marisol Reyes, CEO - 12 years at Genentech, led two INDs.

strengths.claim: Prior IND leadership de-risks the specific milestone this round funds.

weaknesses.claim: No evidence of prior company-building, hiring, or fundraising experience.
The deck names no board, no advisors, and no prior investors.

team.narrative: The bench is two scientists and an acknowledged hole. Dr. Peter Kwan brings genuine academic credibility as a UCSD immunology professor, which supports the mechanism but says nothing about translational execution, and the deck does not state whether he is full-time. The commercial lead role is disclosed as open. Crediting the team for disclosing the gap is fair; the gap is still the gap. For an $4M seed reaching only to IND-enabling toxicology this is survivable, but there is no named regulatory or CMC owner anywhere in the deck.

strengths.claim: Scientific founder holds a named academic appointment in the relevant field.
strengths.quote: Dr. Peter Kwan, CSO - Professor of Immunology, UCSD.

strengths.claim: The team acknowledges its own gap rather than papering over it.
strengths.quote: Commercial lead role is currently open.

weaknesses.claim: No regulatory, CMC, or manufacturing owner is named anywhere in the deck.
CSO's full-time versus advisory status is not stated.
A first commercial hire at seed stage is typically 9-12 months from close.

risks.name: Execution
risks.rationale: The round funds IND-enabling toxicology on an 18-month runway with no named regulatory or CMC owner. The plan is credible; the staffing is not.

evidence.claim: Milestone and runway are stated but not reconciled to named owners.
evidence.quote: Raising $4M seed to complete IND-enabling toxicology.

risks.name: Technology
risks.rationale: Repolarization is shown in vitro only. The gap between an in vitro phenotype switch and in vivo tumor clearance is where most macrophage programs have died.

evidence.claim: Efficacy evidence is limited to in vitro repolarization.
evidence.quote: Repolarizes M2 macrophages to an M1 phenotype in vitro.

risks.name: Commercialization
risks.rationale: No pricing, no payor path, no partner, and no commercial owner. Nothing in the deck addresses who buys this or at what price.

evidence.claim: The deck contains no commercial or pricing slide.

risks.name: Regulatory
risks.rationale: An oral small molecule has a conventional path, but no pre-IND meeting, no indication selection, and no regulatory strategy is described.

evidence.claim: Oral dosing implies a conventional small-molecule regulatory path.
evidence.quote: Oral dosing; no cold chain required.

risks.name: Go-to-Market
risks.rationale: Pre-clinical companies exit via partnership. The deck names no target acquirer, no pharma conversation, and no partnering strategy.

evidence.claim: No partnering or exit path is described.

risks.name: Leadership Scalability
risks.rationale: A two-person scientific team is adequate through tox, but there is no evidence either founder has scaled an organization past that point.

evidence.claim: Team slide lists two people and one open role.

risks.name: Talent Attraction
risks.rationale: San Diego is a deep biotech talent market and the Genentech and UCSD affiliations help, but an unpriced round with no lead weakens the pitch.

evidence.claim: Company is located in an established biotech hub.

biggest_strengths: Founding scientist with a verifiable academic appointment in the exact field.
CEO has led two INDs — the specific milestone this round funds.
Mechanism targets a compartment checkpoint inhibitors demonstrably miss.
Oral small molecule avoids cold chain and biologics manufacturing risk.
biggest_concerns: No in vivo efficacy data whatsoever; the entire case rests on in vitro.
No commercial, regulatory, or CMC owner named anywhere in the deck.
No lead investor and no disclosed valuation or instrument terms.
18-month runway is tight against an IND-enabling tox package.
No IP position is stated — composition of matter is never mentioned.

diligence_questions.question: Who owns the composition-of-matter IP for HLN-101 today, and if it is UCSD, what are the exact license terms and milestone obligations?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: University ownership with unfavorable terms changes the return profile and can block a partnership entirely.

diligence_questions.question: What in vivo data exists today, in which tumor model, and what was the effect size relative to checkpoint-inhibitor control?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: In vitro repolarization is where most macrophage programs look good and then fail. No in vivo signal means this is a science project.

diligence_questions.question: Walk me through the $4M budget line by line against the 18-month runway — what specifically does not get done if tox takes 24 months?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: Reveals whether the milestone-to-runway reconciliation is real or a round number chosen to look fundable.

diligence_questions.question: Is Dr. Kwan full-time, and what does his UCSD appointment allow in terms of time commitment and IP assignment?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: A part-time CSO with a competing academic lab is a different company than the one this deck implies.

diligence_questions.question: Which pharma partners have you spoken to, and what specifically did they say they would need to see to engage?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: The only exit for a pre-clinical asset is partnership. Named, specific feedback separates a real BD process from a hoped-for one.

diligence_questions.question: Who is your first commercial or regulatory hire, when do they start, and is that cost inside the $4M?
diligence_questions.why_it_matters: Tests whether the acknowledged gap has an actual plan and a budget line, or is simply disclosed and deferred.

ic_view.advance_rationale: The science is interesting and the founding scientist is credible, but there is no in vivo data, no stated IP position, no commercial or regulatory owner, and no lead investor. Any one of those is workable at seed; all four together means we would be underwriting a science project at a price nobody has set. Revisit on in vivo efficacy data plus a clean IP answer.

recommendations.action: Generate in vivo efficacy data in at least one syngeneic tumor model.
recommendations.rationale: In vitro repolarization alone will not clear any serious IC.

recommendations.action: Resolve and document the composition-of-matter IP position in writing.
recommendations.rationale: An unstated IP position is assumed to be a bad one.

recommendations.action: Name a regulatory or CMC owner, even fractional, before the raise.
recommendations.rationale: The round funds IND-enabling work with nobody named to run it.

recommendations.action: Add an IP slide stating patent type, jurisdiction, and expiry.
recommendations.rationale: Its absence is the first thing every investor will ask about.

recommendations.action: Replace the in vitro claim with a data slide showing the actual assay.
recommendations.rationale: A claim without a figure reads as a claim you cannot show.

recommendations.action: Reconcile the $4M ask to the 18-month runway line by line on one slide.
recommendations.rationale: Round numbers without a build-up signal the ask was reverse-engineered.

recommendations.action: State the instrument and terms; 'no lead' is not a substitute for terms.
recommendations.rationale: Investors cannot evaluate a deal whose price is undisclosed.

executive_summary: Helion Bio is a San Diego seed-stage biotech raising $4M to take HLN-101, an oral SIRP-alpha antagonist, through IND-enabling toxicology. The mechanism targets tumor-associated macrophages, a compartment checkpoint inhibitors demonstrably miss, and the founding team pairs a Genentech drug developer who has led two INDs with a UCSD immunology professor. That is a real foundation. Against it: efficacy evidence is in vitro only, no IP position is stated anywhere in the deck, the commercial seat is openly vacant, no regulatory or CMC owner is named, and the round has no lead and no disclosed terms. We would not advance this to a partner meeting today. It becomes interesting on in vivo efficacy data in a syngeneic model plus a clean composition-of-matter answer.

grounding_warnings: Grounding: 7/7 FACT claim(s) verified against extracted slide text.
